sourceFrequency_desc: Nominal emitted sound frequency in Hz

formula_wavelength_desc: Wavelength is compressed ahead of motion and expanded behind the source

theoryTitle: Physics of Doppler Effect & Shock Waves
theoryP1: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency or wavelength of a wave in relation to an observer who is in motion relative to the wave source. As the source moves towards the observer, each successive wave crest is emitted from a position closer to the observer than the previous crest, compressing the wavefronts and raising the perceived pitch.
theoryP2: When the source speed equals the speed of sound (Mach 1), circular wave crests cannot escape the source and pile up ahead of it, creating a severe pressure barrier known as the sound barrier.
theoryP3: At supersonic speeds (Mach > 1), the source outruns its own sound waves. The constructive interference of spherical waves forms a conical shockwave front called the Mach cone. When this conical wavefront sweeps across an observer, the abrupt discontinuity in air pressure is heard as a sonic boom.
